meta.name: Suggestions register — one row per proposed improvement, with the decision path and the evidence it needs
meta.purpose: Someone reviewing this page can compare options and choose a path before anything is implemented. Nothing here is implemented silently: every row has a status, a gate and the official sources it depends on.

statusMeaning.awaiting review: Proposed, not chosen. Available for the owner to accept, reject or defer.
statusMeaning.accepted-built: Chosen and already built in this session; the artefact is named in the 'built as' column and is live on the site.
statusMeaning.accepted-proposed-default: Built with a stated default because a policy decision is the owner's, not the system's. The default is labelled and reversible.
statusMeaning.blocked-needs-input: Cannot proceed until the owner answers the linked question in the Questions page.
statusMeaning.rejected: Considered and rejected; the reason is printed so it is not re-proposed.

decisionRules: A suggestion may not contradict a verified official value. If it would, the row links the official source it would contradict and stays 'awaiting review'.
Anything requiring a price, a reward, or a person's judgement is capped at 'accepted-proposed-default' until the owner decides.
No suggestion may introduce a number that is not either (a) computed from official ingested data, or (b) explicitly labelled MODEL/ESTIMATE with its method printed.

suggestions.suggestion: Put every open decision on one page with its evidence, its gap and the cost of deciding wrong, instead of scattering caveats across pages.
suggestions.why: The repository already publishes dozens of correct caveats, but a reader cannot see which ones block a decision. A single register turns caveats into a to-do list.
suggestions.options: A: browsable register (chosen). B: keep caveats per page. C: a PDF brief.
suggestions.cost: Low — generated from a JSON file.
suggestions.risk: A register can look authoritative; mitigated by showing 'blocks' and 'status' rather than a verdict.
suggestions.builtAs: nfl/questions.html + nfl/curated/questions.json

suggestions.suggestion: Score each suggestion by decision value: how much it changes a decision, divided by how much work it is.
suggestions.why: Stops low-value polish outranking the things that actually unblock the system (prices, sample size, ownership of review).
suggestions.options: A: value/effort score shown per row (chosen). B: no ranking.
suggestions.risk: The score is a judgement, so it is labelled JUDGEMENT and the inputs are printed.
suggestions.builtAs: value/effort columns on nfl/suggestions.html

suggestions.suggestion: Publish a fair price (no margin) plus an offered price at a stated hold, and label both, rather than publishing one ambiguous number.
suggestions.why: A single number is unusable: you cannot tell if it is a probability, a price, or a price with juice. Separating fair from offered makes the model auditable.
suggestions.options: A: fair + offered (chosen default). B: fair only. C: offered only.
suggestions.risk: If the hold is not stated per market, the offered price is still ambiguous — hence the hold column.
suggestions.needs: Q02 must be answered by the owner to replace the default hold.
suggestions.builtAs: fair/offered price columns, method printed on nfl/market.html

suggestions.suggestion: Never show a model number without the sample it came from and the uncertainty band.
suggestions.why: A point estimate invites overconfidence. With 8–10 games of official data, the band is wide and that is the honest finding.
suggestions.options: A: value + n + interval (chosen). B: value only.
suggestions.risk: Wide bands look weak; they are accurate.
suggestions.builtAs: n and 90% bootstrap interval on every computed row

suggestions.suggestion: Run a shuffle test that destroys any real edge, and only call a strategy skill-based when its observed score beats the shuffled distribution.
suggestions.why: This is the direct operational answer to 'remove luck from the equation': if the same strategy applied to randomised outcomes scores as well, the result was luck.
suggestions.options: A: shuffle test + minimum sample (chosen). B: raw win rate.
suggestions.cost: Low — pure arithmetic, no external data.
suggestions.risk: A shuffle test controls for outcome randomness but not for data snooping across many strategies; that is why G7 (multiple testing) is a separate gate.
suggestions.builtAs: Monte-Carlo shuffle test, 2000 draws, printed p-value

suggestions.suggestion: Do not rank by win rate. Rank by proper scoring (Brier/log loss) and calibration, and show ROI only where real prices exist.
suggestions.why: Win rate is the most luck-dominated statistic in betting, and ranking by it guarantees the leaderboard rewards variance.
suggestions.options: A: proper scoring + calibration (chosen). B: win rate + ROI.
suggestions.risk: Proper scoring is less intuitive; the site explains it inline.
suggestions.builtAs: leaderboard scoring on nfl/leaderboard.html

suggestions.suggestion: Make the leaderboard paper-only and rank-only by default, with a reward column that reads 'no reward authorised' until the owner sets the rule.
suggestions.why: The owner asked for rewards for top strategies, but a reward rule is a policy decision with money attached. Publishing ranks now and rewards later unblocks everything else.
suggestions.options: A: paper-only ranks first, rewards after policy (chosen). B: define rewards now with invented amounts (rejected).
suggestions.risk: The owner may want rewards immediately — the page therefore shows exactly what one policy decision would unlock.
suggestions.builtAs: 'reward: not authorised' printed on every leaderboard row

suggestions.suggestion: Never multiply leg probabilities for a parlay. Publish the empirical joint probability, the independence product, and the difference.
suggestions.why: The independence product is wrong whenever legs share a game or a player, and the size of the error is exactly what a parlay needs to price.
suggestions.options: A: empirical joint vs independent product, difference shown (chosen). B: independent product only (rejected).
suggestions.cost: Medium — needs a game-keyed join of player logs.
suggestions.risk: Joint probabilities from few games are unstable; suppressed below n=8 shared games.
suggestions.builtAs: nfl/correlation.html, pairwise matrix with n and interval

suggestions.suggestion: Treat the official injury report and the club depth chart as two separate facts, and only call a lineup 'depleted' when both agree and name the replacement.
suggestions.why: Out/Questionable is status, not a lineup. A depth chart is a projection. Combining them into one 'deficiency score' without saying so would be the exact hallucination the owner forbade.
suggestions.options: A: two facts + explicit replacement column (chosen). B: single synthetic severity score (rejected, unverifiable).
suggestions.risk: Depth charts are club-projected and not uniform across clubs (Q12).
suggestions.builtAs: nfl/injuries.html — injury rows joined to depth tier, replacement named only when the chart names one

suggestions.suggestion: Show a per-team 'next man up' depth table: for each position, who starts, who is next, and how many tiers deep the club publishes.
suggestions.why: This is the concrete answer to '2nd, 3rd or 4th string having to replace starters' — it shows the actual published depth rather than asserting deficiency.
suggestions.options: A: full depth table per club (chosen). B: only injured starters (weaker).
suggestions.risk: Clubs publish different tier counts and some say 'Unofficial'.
suggestions.builtAs: nfl/injuries.html depth section

suggestions.suggestion: Separate offensive and defensive deficiency, and show both sides of the same game side by side.
suggestions.why: A missing left tackle hurts the offence's own output; a missing corner helps the opponent's offence. Treating them as one number makes the sign ambiguous.
suggestions.options: A: two columns per game (chosen). B: one net number (rejected — sign ambiguity).
suggestions.risk: Position value is not measured here; the table lists positions, it does not value them.
suggestions.builtAs: offence/defence columns on nfl/injuries.html

suggestions.suggestion: Publish the de-vig method explicitly (multiplicative and additive/power) and show both, because the choice changes the fair price.
suggestions.why: Two-way prices hide a margin; how you remove it changes the fair probability. Showing only one method hides a modelling decision.
suggestions.options: A: both methods + the spread between them (chosen). B: one method (weaker).
suggestions.risk: Neither method is 'correct'; the page says so.
suggestions.builtAs: nfl/market.html de-vig comparator (works on any price pair, demoed on a stated example)

suggestions.suggestion: Do not present any price as 'the market' unless a timestamped, attributable quote is stored. Publish MODEL prices and label them.
suggestions.why: The official NFL pages publish no odds at all (verified: zero odds fields on week, game and stats pages). Claiming a market number would be fabrication.
suggestions.options: A: MODEL label + explicit 'no official price feed' notice (chosen). B: cite a sportsbook page as if official (rejected).
suggestions.risk: The site looks less impressive; it stays true.
suggestions.builtAs: MODEL badge on every non-price number; 'no official price feed' banner on nfl/market.html

suggestions.suggestion: Freeze the gate thresholds before results are seen, and print the freeze date next to the results.
suggestions.why: Thresholds chosen after seeing results are not validation. A printed freeze date makes post-hoc adjustment visible.
suggestions.options: A: pre-registered thresholds with a date (chosen). B: tune later (rejected).
suggestions.risk: The thresholds are still the owner's to change — a change is logged as a new version.
suggestions.builtAs: gate version + frozen date on nfl/validation.html

suggestions.suggestion: Add a multiple-testing guard so that testing 40 strategies cannot manufacture a winner.
suggestions.why: With enough strategies, one will look skilful by chance. The guard raises the bar as the number of tested strategies grows.
suggestions.options: A: Benjamini–Hochberg style guard (chosen). B: none (rejected).
suggestions.risk: Conservative — some real edges will be held back; that is the point.
suggestions.builtAs: false-discovery guard on nfl/validation.html

suggestions.suggestion: Ingest official data in CI rather than transcribing it by hand, and commit the raw fetch report with every run.
suggestions.why: Hand transcription is where invented values come from. A committed fetch report makes every table row traceable to a URL and a time.
suggestions.options: A: CI ingest + fetch report (chosen). B: manual transcription (rejected).
suggestions.risk: CI runners reach the official hosts; the dev sandbox does not, so local runs cannot refresh data.
suggestions.builtAs: .github/workflows/nfl-data.yml + nfl/data/fetch-report.json

suggestions.suggestion: Keep the new section additive: a separate `nfl/` shelf with its own navigation, so the existing planner pages and their generators are untouched.
suggestions.why: Two sessions already own the root pages. An additive section cannot break their build, and a reviewer can ignore it entirely.
suggestions.options: A: additive section (chosen). B: rewrite root pages (rejected — conflicts with other sessions).
suggestions.risk: Two navigations on the site; mitigated by an explicit link in both directions.
suggestions.builtAs: nfl/*.html with its own nav; one nav entry added to the root pages

suggestions.suggestion: Put an 'unverified' badge on every value the official source did not publish, and leave the cell empty rather than blank-looking.
suggestions.why: An empty cell is ambiguous: it could mean zero, missing, or not checked. An explicit badge removes the ambiguity.
suggestions.options: A: explicit badge + em dash (chosen). B: empty cell (rejected).
suggestions.risk: Visually noisy; accepted as the cost of honesty.
suggestions.builtAs: unverified badge rule in nfl/tools/build_nfl.py, asserted by nfl/tools/verify_nfl.py

suggestions.suggestion: Assign a named reviewer for the suggestions register and require a written reason on every accept/reject.
suggestions.why: Without an owner, a register is decoration. Without reasons, the same rejected idea returns next session.
suggestions.options: A: named reviewer + reason (chosen). B: no owner.
suggestions.risk: It is the owner's time; the page therefore batches decisions and shows the decision value of each.
suggestions.builtAs: reviewer column left blank and marked 'unassigned' on nfl/suggestions.html

suggestions.suggestion: Store an immutable snapshot of every price the owner records, with book and timestamp, so closing-line value can be computed later.
suggestions.why: CLV is the fastest-validating measure of skill, and it is impossible to compute retroactively without stored quotes.
suggestions.options: A: append-only quote ledger (schema proposed). B: compute CLV from memory (rejected).
suggestions.risk: Entering prices is manual — this is the one place manual input is unavoidable unless a licensed feed is bought.
suggestions.builtAs: ledger schema published, no data

suggestions.suggestion: Rank single bets, parlays and player-prop combos in three separate competitions rather than one leaderboard.
suggestions.why: They have different variance and different data requirements; pooling them lets a lucky parlay outrank a well-calibrated single.
suggestions.options: A: three boards (chosen). B: one pooled board (rejected).
suggestions.risk: Sparser boards; mitigated by showing n on every row.
suggestions.builtAs: three leaderboards on nfl/leaderboard.html

suggestions.suggestion: Publish an explicit 'what we do not have' block on the market page rather than a footnote.
suggestions.why: The most important information about a betting page is what it cannot see. A footnote is read by nobody.
suggestions.options: A: top-of-page block (chosen). B: footnote (rejected).
suggestions.risk: Makes the page look incomplete — it is.
suggestions.builtAs: 'What we do not have' block on nfl/market.html and nfl/index.html
